title: Polio left her leg impaired. Her husband threw her out. She won India's first para-athletics Commonwealth gold. October 12, 2026.
excerpt: From a cyclone that killed 116 instead of tens of thousands, to a village doctor who never left his old patients behind, October 12's five stories are about systems and people that got stronger precisely where they were once weakest.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about strength built at the exact point of a known weakness - a coastline that used to have no warning system, a scientist whose lab discoveries used to stay in the lab, a cardiologist whose practice could have stayed entirely in New Jersey, a power grid that used to have no way to store renewable energy, and a woman whose body and marriage both once seemed to have broken her future.

October 12, 2014: a cyclone with 185 km/h winds hit India's coast. It killed 116 people - not tens of thousands

Cyclone Hudhud made landfall near Visakhapatnam at peak intensity, the first cyclone to cross that coast in October since 1985. India moved roughly 400,000 people out of its path before it arrived - the same early-warning system that didn't exist 150 years earlier, when the Calcutta Cyclone killed tens of thousands with no warning at all.

He holds 65 US patents and won nine R&D 100 Awards. In 2026, he was named Researcher of the Year

Dr. M. Parans Paranthaman, educated at Madurai Kamaraj University and IIT Madras before joining Oak Ridge National Laboratory, was named R&D World's 2026 Researcher of the Year for a career spent turning lab discoveries - batteries, superconductor wires, lithium extraction - into deployed technology.

A US cardiologist still runs free medical camps in the Jharkhand village he grew up in

Dr. Avinash Gupta, born in Karum village, Ranchi, has practiced cardiology in New Jersey since 1994 - and through PRAN-BJANA has led over 150 free medical camps in rural Bihar and Jharkhand, on top of leading COVID-era vaccination drives for Indian-Americans back in the US.

India just finished a 1,000 MW battery that isn't a battery at all

THDC India completed the 1,000 MW Tehri Pumped Storage Project in April 2026 - storing energy by pumping water uphill when power is cheap, then releasing it downhill at peak demand, giving India's growing solar and wind capacity a way to firm up without a single battery cell.

Polio left her leg permanently impaired. Her first husband threw her and her daughters out of their home. She didn't find her sport until she was 34

Sharmila Dhankar discovered para athletics in 2020 after decades of hardship, and at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, at age 40, won gold in women's shot put F57 with a season-best 9.81m throw - India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold in para-athletics.

Five stories, one thread: a coast that learned to warn its people in time, a scientist who learned to get his discoveries out of the lab, a doctor who never stopped treating the village he left, a grid that finally learned to store the power it generates, and a woman who found her sport only after everything else had already tried to break her. All of it got stronger exactly where it used to be weak.
